newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore export rise has little impact on shares.
newsitem.headline: Singapore export rise has little impact on shares.

text.p: A surprise rise in Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in October had little impact on share prices which were driven upwards instead by a strong overnight showing from Wall Street, dealers said on Wednesday.
The export figures showed a 1.1 percent year-on-year rise in exports, beating the market forecast of a 1.4 percent fall.
They were "a positive sign, but no more than that," one dealer said.
Price rises in Singapore's morning session were more influenced by the New York stock exchange's overnight record close of 6,397.60 he said.
Singapore shares had rallied through the morning, pushing the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index up 20.85 points to 2,191.03 at the 0430 GMT lunchtime close.
Traded volume was a healthy 94.59 million shares, producing 217 gainers 65 losers. Dealers said the morning activity reflected a more optimistic mood in the market.
